blocking_defects.defect: B's board treats s1 and s2 as the Chevron pilot (DroneLife c3, c4, c17) and switches to 'Illustration of EPA's method, generic inspector' at s3, through a source-example transition. But the renderer draws the same generic certified inspector in the pilot scenes. In s1 room-window, restingPerson turns her toward the window as the pilot drone's hood opens and it lifts off (registry room-window subject_ids include s1-inspector). In s2 room-monitor she watches the companies' alert on her tablet (s2-inspector). The person, room and window then continue unchanged into the EPA-method scenes, and the s9 window returns to the same pad. The s1 and s2 chip reads only 'Illustration. Generic drone and inspector'. The continuous person therefore cancels the s3 disclosure. The likely false inference is that Chevron's Permian pilot drones were already watched and confirmed by a certified inspector on site, under this approval. No source reports that: DroneLife describes monitoring and AI analytics from remote control centers, and EPA's letter describes review of collected footage under the approved method. Required correction: keep the EPA-method inspector out of the pilot scenes, for example by starting B's room story at s3. Alternatively, stage s1 and s2 with a visibly different, disclosed role and place, such as an operator at a remote control center as DroneLife describes, with a chip that says so. Do not return the review room's window to the pilot pad as if it were the same site, or disclose it as the illustrated method's generic pad.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: The intended chain, reconstructed from the executable code: In an inspection room a seated inspector turns to her window as a drone station's hood opens on the pad outside and the drone lifts off. On her tablet the companies' blue 'Anomaly' flag rises on a pump-pressure reading, tagged 'The companies say'. An approval letter slides onto her desk and takes its date and Approved stamps while she watches and taps a pen. On her wall monitor's live feed the drone flies to a valve ring and an infrared view opens. At the review screen she traces the shimmer, presses green and flicks a follow-up tag to the valve. She reads the protocol title, where AI is highlighted once, then the separate program's delay and proposed rescission. Finally she re-presses her green mark beside an empty AI box as the station closes outside her window.
story_review.opening_to_ending: B opens and closes on the same person, which makes 'who decides' visibly human throughout. Because that same person is also present in the pilot scenes and the separate-program scenes, the film implies she belongs to Chevron's pilot and to the program being rescinded. That blurs the limits the ending must keep clear.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (11.44 s). The board marks this cut as a switch of source example to EPA's method, but the same inspector, desk and window continue straight through it, so the picture does not change example.
